summary: M2-S05 (Case OWD Private + criteria-based sharing rule opening Support cases to Tier 2) passed all 3 runnable declared acceptance tests plus both always-on structural checks: xml (2/2 parse), manifest (SharingRules:Case two-way consistent), and the declared checker skills/admin/sharing-and-visibility/scripts/check_sharing_model.py --manifest-dir artefacts (build scope, exit 0, resolved exactly the 1 object OWD the step's own test description claims it would at build scope, versus 0 at step scope). check-outputs: ok, no missing/empty/malformed. 1 manual test (B01+B04) deferred to the M2 gate -- Given/When/Then shape present with a named observable outcome, so usable, not ticked here. Grep-confirmed directly from disk: exactly one sharingCriteriaRules block, sharedTo group is Support_Tier_2 only, no rule names the Billing record type or Billing_Team, the Private OWD lives on M1-S01's Case.object-meta.xml, and no Sharing.settings/*.settings-meta.xml file exists anywhere under artefacts/ (the one textual hit for the string is prose in M2-S04's queue-retirement-runbook.md, not a settings file). Status set to tested.
confidence_rationale: Step 7 rubric, HIGH row: every declared test either ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed. No MEDIUM trigger fired -- no command test was refused, no coverage-gap exclusion was needed (the only metadata file present is a SharingRules container, which has a standalone file), and check-outputs reported no missing, empty or malformed declared output. No LOW trigger fired -- the one declared checker existed and ran, the artefact directory holds 4 files (2 XML, 2 markdown), and every exit code was captured to tests/M2-S05/.

process_observations.observation: The build-scope declaration on the checker test did what its own description says it would: check_sharing_model.py --manifest-dir artefacts resolved 1 object OWD (Case, from M1-S01's Case.object-meta.xml) and scored the grant against it, rather than the vacuous 0-object-OWD, always-exit-0 result a step-scoped run over artefacts/M2-S05 alone would have produced. Confirms the step's own reproduced-on-a-fixture claim in its acceptance_tests[0].description.

Every negative assertion the manual test and deploy-order.md's 'Elements this step could NOT ground' section make about this rule set held on direct inspection of the artefact: exactly one sharingCriteriaRules block, one sharedTo group (Support_Tier_2), and 'Billing' appearing only inside the rule's free-text description -- never as a criteriaItems.value, a sharedTo.group, or a second rule.

package.xml manifests this rule under the container form (SharingRules : Case) while the step's own cited skill reference (sharing-and-visibility/references/metadata-examples.md section 6, quoted verbatim in deploy-order.md Decision 1) recommends the rule-type form (SharingCriteriaRule : Case.Support_Cases_To_Tier_2). deploy-order.md records this as a deliberate, reasoned divergence -- the container form is what this agent's own file-name-derived manifest check (Step 3, devops/salesforce-dx-project-structure) can cover, and the rule-type form would leave the file uncovered by that same logic. Both forms are reported to deploy the same file; neither this run's manifest check nor its checker run treats this as a failure, consistent with this run's own instruction to report it as a plan-text observation rather than tick or fail it.

The risk checklist in case-visibility-model.md leaves two boxes explicitly unticked at this point in the build: 'Public group membership exists in the target org' (it does not -- GroupMember rows for Support_Tier_2 are a post-deploy data step tracked in M2-S04's queue-retirement-runbook.md section 6) and 'Access proved with a UserRecordAccess query' (deferred to M5, where a sandbox exists). Neither is this step's acceptance test to close -- both are named, owned, and tracked elsewhere in the build -- but a green tested status here does not by itself mean the grant is live for any user yet.
M2-S05 is now tested but its documentation (workbook rows, traceability entries, decisions log) has not yet been updated to reflect this test run.
process_observations.followup_reason: Because the doc keeper is the agent that carries a tested step's evidence into PLAN.md, the workbook and traceability.md, and this run performed no documentation writes.
